    TVC-REQ-001
    L1. Ease of Integration
    UID: TVC-REQ-001
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Functional
    Applicable subsystem: Airframe, Propulsion, Actuation, Recovery
    Subteam owner: Systems, Structures, Electrical
    Individual owner: Systems Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: Pre-Launch
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Demonstration
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-004 Rapid Launch Turnaround
    RELATIONS (Child):
    • TVC-REQ-039 Battery performance and life
    Statement:

    The vehicle shall be fully integrated, launched, and recovered within 2 hours under nominal conditions.
    Rationale:

    This requirement decomposes TVC-MO-004, specifically focusing on the vehicle, and giving a specific timeframe for complete turnaround. Most launch sites are open from 10 AM to 4 PM, so 2 hours is the absolute maximum each launch may take. This does not take into account failures, which are varied and more specifically specified in the Concept of Operations documents.
    TVC-REQ-002
    L1. Flight Computer Fire Wire
    UID: TVC-REQ-002
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Functional
    Applicable subsystem: Avionics, Recovery, Power
    Subteam owner: Electrical
    Individual owner: Electrical Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: Parachute Descent
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Test
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-006 Recover Vehicle Safely
    RELATIONS (Child):
    • TVC-REQ-008 PCB Fire Wire Protection
    Statement:

    The on board rocket avionics shall have the ability to set off fire wire, with at least 3 channels available to fire.
    Rationale:

    This derived requirement ensures the rocket avionics will be able to support redundant single-deploy recovery, along with an extra channel to support landing operations in the future, such as fire wire to release landing legs.
    TVC-REQ-003
    L1. Flight Computer Data Logging
    UID: TVC-REQ-003
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Functional
    Applicable subsystem: Avionics, Power, Flight_Software
    Subteam owner: Electrical, Software
    Individual owner: Electrical Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: All
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Test
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-005 Capture Flight Data
    Statement:

    The Flight Computer shall log all determined relevant flight data on an onboard SD-Card. This includes all raw sensor data (IMU, Barometer, other peripherals), relevant state estimation outputs (State Vector), actuator command outputs, individual control outputs, timestamps for each set of data, and current state of the state machine.
    Rationale:

    This decomposes TVC-MO-005 to apply to flight computer onboard data logging, along with a more specific set of data to collect.
    TVC-REQ-004
    L1. Relevant Telemetry Data
    UID: TVC-REQ-004
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Functional
    Applicable subsystem: Avionics, Power, Flight_Software, Ground_Systems
    Subteam owner: Electrical, Software
    Individual owner: Electrical Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: All
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Test
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-005 Capture Flight Data
    Statement:

    The flight computer shall send relevant flight data to a ground station via telemetry data packets. This includes state estimation outputs (State Vector), actuator commands outputs, individual control outputs, timestamps since launch, and the current state of the state machine.
    Rationale:

    This decomposes TVC-MO-005 to apply to telemetry to the ground station, along with more specific information on what to send.
    TVC-REQ-005
    L1. Gimbal Minimum Angle
    UID: TVC-REQ-005
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Physical
    Applicable subsystem: Actuation
    Subteam owner: Structures
    Individual owner: Structures Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: Powered Ascent
    Flight attempt: Flight 1
    Open item status: TBD
    Resolution owner: Controls Lead
    Resolution plan: Controls subteam will use a completed GNCSim architecture, with an integrated model/simulation of the gimbal, in order to determine the minimum gimbal angle. The simulation shall prove that the minimum gimbal angle (along with other gimbal properties) provided allows the rocket to maintain attitude under environmental conditions. Simulation results must be produced before the gimbal CDR. If GNCSim is not finished/integrated in time to complete this task, off the shelf tools such as aeroVECTOR will be used in replacement.
    Resolution due date: October 16th
    Verification method: Demonstration
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-001 Maintain Powered Attitude
    Statement:

    The minimum actuation angle the gimbal shall be physically capable of is [TBD_GimAngle] degrees, in all directions (360 degrees).
    Rationale:

    Based on results from GNCSim dynamic analysis, this will help establish the minimum ange the gimbal is capable of in order for the rocket to be physically capable of maintaining attitude, a fundamental function the rocket must have in order to meet system goals.

    TVC-REQ-008
    L2. PCB Fire Wire Protection
    UID: TVC-REQ-008
    Level: L2
    Requirement type: Safety
    Applicable subsystem: Avionics
    Subteam owner: Electrical
    Individual owner: Electrical Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: Pre-Launch
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Inspection
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-REQ-002 Flight Computer Fire Wire
    Statement:

    The flight computer shall support a physical inhibit/enable switch for the fire wire, with physical on-board feedback of inhibit/enable status that the microntroller can read.
    Rationale:

    Inhibiting the fire wire switch is an important safety feature to ensure safe operations while handling the rocket up until launch operations. Feedback ensures the team is aware of the state of the fire wire.
    TVC-REQ-009

    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Inspection
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-004 Rapid Launch Turnaround
    Statement:

    For major board circuitry, such as the recovery circuit, it shall be possible to physically check voltage using test points on the board. Important power lines, recovery circuitry, microntroller debugging, interfaces (CAN, JTAG), and more should include test points.
    Rationale:

    This is both an important board design feature to allow for debugging in the case of failures during testing, and any last minute debugging required on the launch site.

    For important flight computer debugging interfaces, such as flashing code and MCU reset, these interfaces shall be accessible during all pre-launch activities until the rocket is placed on the launch rail/pad.

    TVC-REQ-014
    L1. Max Dry Rocket Mass
    UID: TVC-REQ-014
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Physical
    Applicable subsystem: Airframe, Propulsion, Actuation, Avionics, Power, Recovery
    Subteam owner: Structures, Electrical
    Individual owner: Systems Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: All
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Inspection
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MC-001 Vehicle Altitude Condition
    RELATIONS (Child):
    • TVC-REQ-015 Max Gimbal Mass
    • TVC-REQ-016 Max Avionics Mass
    • TVC-REQ-017 Max "other" mass
    Statement:

    The max dry mass of the rocket (mass without motors) shall be a maximum of 1050 grams.
    Rationale:

    A simple, 1D simulation was put together in order to Validate this requirement. That simulation can be found in docs/Configuration/TVC-REQ-013 folder. This simple 1-D simulation is required, as OpenRocket cannot properly simulate the full flight of an unstable rocket. The mass of the rocket in the simulation was adjusted to find the absolute maximum mass that allowed for around 50 feet of altitude gain, with some tolerance. This ensures the rocket, assuming a mostly vertical flight, will not reach the ground before motor burnout.
    TVC-REQ-015
    L2. Max Gimbal Mass
    UID: TVC-REQ-015
    Level: L2
    Requirement type: Physical
    Applicable subsystem: Actuation
    Subteam owner: Structures
    Individual owner: Structures Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: All
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Inspection
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-REQ-014 Max Dry Rocket Mass
    Statement:

    The max mass of all gimbal components shall be a maximum of 350 grams.
    Rationale:

    Using previous program experience. From Scarlet (Gimbaled 2024-2025) the mass of the gimbal was ~200 grams, but increased to ~800 grams on HPRTVC. Seeing as the architecture of Gimbaled TVC (Being low powered) matches Scarlet, but has greater restrictions (Accuracy, Speed, etc..) the mass is taken from Scarlet, with increased tolerance to allow for improved design.
    TVC-REQ-016
    L2. Max Avionics Mass
    UID: TVC-REQ-016
    Level: L2
    Requirement type: Physical
    Applicable subsystem: Avionics, Power

    Verification method: Inspection
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-REQ-014 Max Dry Rocket Mass
    Statement:

    The max mass of all avionics components shall be a maximum of 450 grams.
    Rationale:

    Using previous program experience. From Scarlet (Gimbaled 2024-2025) the mass of the avionics was ~500 grams, but increased to ~800 grams on HPRTVC. In order to accomodate other rocket changes, such as an improved gimbal, the mass budget for the avionics bay is slightly reduced. This is assumed to be practical, considering electrical team goals to make a lightweight, compact flight computer.

    The max mass of all non-gimbal, non-avionics components shall be a maximum of 250 grams.

    Considering TVC-REQ-014 and TVC-REQ-015, the remaining mass in order to meet TVC-REQ-013 is 250g. Seeing as the remaining mass includes airframe, nosecone, and recovery, this is likely a reasonable constraint, especially considering previous program experience.
    TVC-REQ-018
    L1. Specific Controls Shutoff Conditions
    UID: TVC-REQ-018
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Functional
    Applicable subsystem: Avionics, Flight_Software
    Subteam owner: Controls
    Individual owner: Controls Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: Powered Ascent
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: TBD
    Resolution owner: Controls Lead
    Resolution plan: Once a completed GNCSim architecture has been put together, and the Gimbaled TVC rocket is ready to simulate, a variety of unsafe conditions should be simulated via Monte Carlo (Rocket Angle from Vertical, Angular rates in Pitch, Yaw, and Roll). For each of these factors, a maximum safe condition shall be decided, based on whether the rocket can recover from the condition by the end of the burn of the motor. Because the values are a small change in software, this can be resolved later on in the design cycle. Additionally, GNCSim should simulate what happens after controls shutoff. GNCSim should consider cases of return back to 0, return back to 0 and cut power, just cutting power, etc...
    Resolution due date: December 1st
    Verification method: Test
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-008 Controls Shutoff Condition
    Statement:

    The rocket controls shall be turned off when unsafe conditions are reached. Unsafe conditions include: (1) Rocket [TBD_UnsafeDeg] degrees from vertical, (2) Rocket has [TBD_UnsafeRate] angular rate in Pitch/Yaw, (3) Rocket has [TBD_UnsafeRate2] angular rate in Roll. Controls shutoff invovles actuating the gimbal to the known 0 position, then cutting power from the gimbal actuators.
    Rationale:

    This meets the parent requirement, ensuring that controls are shutoff once angle, or rates, are too high to recover from. At this point, it is assumed the controls are not working as expected, and likely are contributing to rocket unsafe conditions.

    • TVC-REQ-021 GNCSim Aerodynamics Requirements
    Statement:

    The controls team shall develop a full, closed-loop model of the Gimbaled TVC rocket in GNCSim in order find and tune the closed loop controls for the vehicle.
    Rationale:

    In order to derive a control loop algorithm, the team must use GNCSim to model the rocket, the control algorithm, and use GNCSim to evaluate the control algorithm (Stability, Response Time, Steady State Error, etc...)

    TVC-REQ-023
    L1. Control Loop Overall Architecture
    UID: TVC-REQ-023
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Design Constraint
    Applicable subsystem: Avionics, Flight_Software
    Subteam owner: Software
    Individual owner: Software Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: All
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Test
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-010 Onboard state machine
    Statement:

    Every state in the state machine shall have clearly defined entry and exit criteria. Implementation of the entry and exit criteria shall match the criteri and prevent any invalid state transitions (Ex: Transitions to other states when unintended)
    Rationale:

    Each state in a state machine must have a way to enter and exit. It is flight critical that the rocket does not enter a state when it is not intended for it to do so. For example, if the rocket were to enter the state pertaining to recovery prematurely, and prematurely deploy the parachute before motor burnout, that would be detrimental to the mission objectives.
    TVC-REQ-024
    L1. Motor Burn Time
    UID: TVC-REQ-024
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Physical
    Applicable subsystem: Propulsion
    Subteam owner: Systems
    Individual owner: Systems Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: Powered Ascent
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Inspection
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-001 Maintain Powered Attitude
    RELATIONS (Child):
    • TVC-REQ-025 Gimbaled TVC Motor Selection
    Statement:

    The motor shall have a burn time of at least three seconds.
    Rationale:

    In order to demonstratably show the rocket controlling its attitude, it must have a long enough burn time to give the control system time to correct any errors in atttitude. Assuming it takes the rocket ~1 second to clear the launch rail, a minimum of a three second burn time gives the rocket ~2 seconds to correct any errors in attitude. From previous program experience, this should be enough to discernebly notice whether the control system is reacting to the other, along with collecting enough data to do so.
    TVC-REQ-025
    L2. Gimbaled TVC Motor Selection
    UID: TVC-REQ-025

    • TVC-MO-007 Vehicle Structural Integrity
    Statement:

    The motor shall be properly constrained in the rocket, where it does not fall out under normal pre-launch activities, at all times from pre-launch to end of the mision.
    Rationale:

    Constraining the motor is important to ensure flight operations go smoothly and the motor can properly transfer force to the vehicle.
    TVC-REQ-027
    L1. Parachute Release Conditions
    UID: TVC-REQ-027
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Functional
    Applicable subsystem: Recovery, Flight_Software, Avionics
    Subteam owner: Structures
    Individual owner: Structures Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: Parachute Descent
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Test
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-006 Recover Vehicle Safely
    Statement:

    The recovery system shall be deployed at the minimum expected velocity of the rocket, which is also apogee. Once the barometer data has no readings greater than a previous reading for >0.5 seconds, the fire wire should be set off.
    Rationale:

    The parachute should be deployed at minumum velocity (apogee) to reduce loads on the chute and other recovery hardware. This condition can be most easily read by the barometer.
    TVC-REQ-028
    L1. Rocket Airframe Material
    UID: TVC-REQ-028
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Design Constraint
    Applicable subsystem: Airframe
    Subteam owner: Structures
    Individual owner: Structures Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: All
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Analysis
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-007 Vehicle Structural Integrity
    Statement:

    The rocket shall use cardboard as the material for its airframe.
    Rationale:

    Carboard is a lightweight material common for Low Power rockets. It is less dense than blue tube, and from previous program experience it is well equipped to experience the expected loads
    TVC-REQ-029
    L1. Rocket Airframe and Nosecone Material
    UID: TVC-REQ-029
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Design Constraint
    Applicable subsystem: Airframe
    Subteam owner: Structures
    Individual owner: Structures Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: All
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Analysis
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MC-002 NAR Material Standards
    Statement:

    The rocket shall use no metal in the cardboard airframe, in the nosecone, and any gimbal components that are not constrained in the body tube.
    Rationale:

    NAR regulations do not allow metal in the externals of the rocket, this requirement decomposes the parent requirement to apply to specific components.
    TVC-REQ-030
    L1. Range Safety Constraints
    UID: TVC-REQ-030
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Safety
    Applicable subsystem: N_A
    Subteam owner: Controls
    Individual owner: Controls Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: All
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: TBD
    Resolution owner: Controls Lead
    Resolution plan: The requirement lists the resolution plan. GNCSim shall simulate the rocket dispersion under thrust to close this requirement.
    Resolution due date: September 30th, 2026
    Verification method: Analysis
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MC-003 Range Safety Analysis
    RELATIONS (Child):
    • TVC-REQ-032 Ground Ignition System
    Statement:

    The rocket launch range, [TBD_LaunchRange], shall be derived via Monte Carlo flight dynamic simulation. The vehicle's max TVC limit, aerodynamic load range, maximum determined failire modes should be considered. For range safety, altitude shall not be a consideration (At any range, the rocket is deemed unsafe, even if at a higher altitude)
    Rationale:

    This requirement decomposes the parent requirement by specifically requiring dynamic analysis to find launch range, and setting specific constraints.
    TVC-REQ-031
    L1. Launch Rail Usage
    UID: TVC-REQ-031
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Safety
    Applicable subsystem: Ground_Systems
    Subteam owner: Structures
    Individual owner: Structures Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: All
    Flight attempt: Flights 1-3
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Inspection
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MC-003 Range Safety Analysis
    Statement:

    The mission shall use a team-built launch rail and team-built method to ignite the rocket, where both can be placed wherever without any problem.
    Rationale:

    This requirement ensures range safety will be met by allowing the rocket to be placed anywhere on the launch site.
    TVC-REQ-032
    L2. Ground Ignition System
    UID: TVC-REQ-032
    Level: L2
    Requirement type: Safety
    Applicable subsystem: Ground_Systems
    Subteam owner: Structures, Electrical, Software
    Individual owner: Structures Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: All
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: TBR
    Resolution owner: Electrical
    Resolution plan: Once launch range has been established, the exact microcontroller and wireless communication method will be decided. For example, if launch range is expected to be over 300 feet, the Raspberry Pi wifi capabilities may not be sufficient.
    Resolution due date: October 31st, 2026
    Verification method: Inspection
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-REQ-030 Range Safety Constraints
    Statement:

    The team-built rocket ignition method shall use a Commerical off the shelf (COTS) micrcontroller (Such as Raspberry Pi), using an e-match and supporting components (Ex: Wiring). The micrcontroller must have built in wireless communication capabilities or include a component (such as an external radio) that allows it to do so. The wireless communication method shall be: [TBD_WirelessCommMethod].
    Rationale:

    Using a COTS microcontroller reduces complexity of the ground ignition system, and wireless communication is a must-have to allow the launch range to be met. The exact method of sending the ignition signal is TBD depending on how large the range actually is.
    TVC-REQ-033
    L1. Removable launch rail
    UID: TVC-REQ-033
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Design Constraint
    Applicable subsystem: Ground_Systems
    Subteam owner: Structures
    Individual owner: Structures Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: All
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Inspection
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-011 Removing launch rail
    Statement:

    The designed team-built launchpad shall have a removable launch rail.
    Rationale:

    This ensures the team must only design/manufacture one launchpad, that is both applicable for launches with and without using a launch rail.
    TVC-REQ-034
    L1. Black Powder Used
    UID: TVC-REQ-034
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Physical
    Applicable subsystem: Recovery
    Subteam owner: Structures
    Individual owner: Structures Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: All
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: TBD
    Resolution owner: Structures
    Resolution plan: Black Powder testing, where the entire recovery system is placed in the rokcet tube and black powder is ejected on the ground, will determine the sufficient amount of black powder.
    Resolution due date: October 30th, 2026
    Verification method: Demonstration
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-006 Recover Vehicle Safely
    Statement:

    The rocket shall use a sufficient amount of black powder in order to effectively release the parachute system, [TBD_BlackPowder] grams at a minimum.
    Rationale:

    An insufficient amount of black powder will lead to a stuck nosecone and a failure to effectively recover the rocket.
    TVC-REQ-035
    L1. Recovery Electrical Independence
    UID: TVC-REQ-035
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Design Constraint
    Applicable subsystem: Recovery, Avionics
    Subteam owner: Electrical
    Individual owner: Electrical Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: Parachute Descent
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Inspection
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-006 Recover Vehicle Safely
    Statement:

    The flight computer's recovery electrical power system shall operate independently from other board functions such as primariy flight control, using dedicated poewr rails and isolated distribution paths.
    Rationale:

    Effective recovery means ensuring the fire wire is never set off accidentally. This is also a safety concern. Power system independence reduces the chance of a design error causing current/voltage surges.
    TVC-REQ-036
    L1. Recovery Parachute Sizing
    UID: TVC-REQ-036
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Physical
    Applicable subsystem: Recovery
    Subteam owner: Structures
    Individual owner: Structures Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: Parachute Descent
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Inspection
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-006 Recover Vehicle Safely
    Statement:

    The descent rate of the rocket shall be under 20 feet per second while under parachute
    Rationale:

    20 feet per second is model rocketry standard parachute descent rate to ensure a safe recovery and low ground hit speed.
    TVC-REQ-037
    L1. Harness/Wiring Effective Routing
    UID: TVC-REQ-037
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Physical
    Applicable subsystem: Airframe, Avionics, Actuation, Recovery
    Subteam owner: Structures
    Individual owner: Structures Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: All
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Inspection
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-007 Vehicle Structural Integrity
    Statement:

    All wiring in the rocket shall be tied off (mounted) at a maximum distance between ties of 0.75 inches.
    Rationale:

    NASA STD-8739.4 gives standards for wire harnesses, and tells us that at a wire diameter of 0.25 inches or less, maximum tie off distance should be 0.75 inches. While not all wire gauges have been decided, it is likely that most wries will end up smaller than 0.25 inches, so this requirement is applied to the entire rocket. This is decomposed from TVC-MO-007, where wires coming loose is considerd "disassembly".
    TVC-REQ-038
    L1. Launch State Transition
    UID: TVC-REQ-038
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Functional
    Applicable subsystem: Avionics, Flight_Software
    Subteam owner: Software
    Individual owner: Software Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: Pre-Launch
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Test
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-010 Onboard state machine
    Statement:

    The flight software shall detect launch, and once it does transition the state machine to powered ascent (Where active controls will be active). The conditions to detect launch shall be: Acceleration above +0.5G for 50 ms.
    Rationale:

    According to OpenRocket, the thrust:weight ratio off the pad is ~2. Removing gravity, this is 1G acceleration. Applying a scaling factor of 0.5, which balances sensitivty and gives a tolerance for acceleration, this gives a launch condition of +0.5G. 50ms ensures that random disturbances do not trigger the launch (Control loop runs at >20Hz), while also ensuring that launch is detected quickly, reducing time when the rocket does not control itself.
    TVC-REQ-039
    L2. Battery performance and life
    UID: TVC-REQ-039
    Level: L2
    Requirement type: Performance
    Applicable subsystem: Avionics, Power
    Subteam owner: Electrical
    Individual owner: Electrical Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: Pre-Launch
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Analysis
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-REQ-001 Ease of Integration
    Statement:

    The vehicle battery shall last at least two hours under nominal expected operating conditions. Nominal operating conditions include power being on for 2 hours, with at least half an hour of actuation testing and other misc. testing and launch activities.
    Rationale:

    In order to provide turnaround in two hours, it will be difficult to do so if having to replace the battery often. Ensuring the battery needs to be replaced, at a maximum, once between flights ensures there is no time wasted between launch turnaround time.
    TVC-REQ-040
    L1. Overcurrent/Reverse Polarity Protections
    UID: TVC-REQ-040
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Functional
    Applicable subsystem: Avionics, Power
    Subteam owner: Electrical
    Individual owner: Electrical Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: Pre-Launch
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Demonstration
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-012 Protection against accidents
    Statement:

    The flight computer, and other supporting boards, shall have protection against overcurrent and reverse voltage.
    Rationale:

    A common club mistake has been plugging incorrect batteries/reversing battery connectors. To help prevent these mistakes crippling launch, boards must not be affected by incorrect power being plugged in.
    TVC-REQ-041
    L1. Labeling Wires Before Launch
    UID: TVC-REQ-041
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Functional
    Applicable subsystem: Avionics, Power, Actuation
    Subteam owner: Electrical
    Individual owner: Electrical Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: Pre-Launch
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Inspection
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-012 Protection against accidents
    Statement:

    Every single cable that is used for launch, ranging from servo cables for the actuators, to CAN connection, to JTAG connectors, shall be labeled before leaving for the launch site.
    Rationale:

    Cables can be plugged in incorrectly, and labeling all of them beforehand gives time to double check connections beforehand and prevent on-site quick decisions from de-railing launches. This also helps improve turnaround as less time is spent deciding exactly which cables need to be plugged in where.
    TVC-REQ-042
    L1. Gimbal Replaceable Motor Case
    UID: TVC-REQ-042
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Design Constraint
    Applicable subsystem: Propulsion, Actuation
    Subteam owner: Structures
    Individual owner: Structures Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: Pre-Launch
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Demonstration
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-012 Protection against accidents
    Statement:

    The gimbal design shall use an easily replaceable motor holder.
    Rationale:

    The motor holder, historically, has warped under heating from the motor. Instead of requiring the motor holder to be designed to handle the heat, this requirement allows warping, and replacing the motor in the engine is a motor of replacing the motor and holder as a unit.
    TVC-REQ-043
    L1. No last Minute Changes
    UID: TVC-REQ-043
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Functional
    Applicable subsystem: N_A
    Subteam owner: Systems
    Individual owner: Systems Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: Pre-Launch
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Inspection
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-012 Protection against accidents
    RELATIONS (Child):
    • TVC-REQ-044 Flight Software Changes
    Statement:

    The rocket and supporting systems shall prevent any last minute changes made to the design, structures, flight software, avionics, etc... Note: Last minute is defined differently for different subsystems.
    Rationale:

    Last minute changes are easy ways to introduce errors into the rocket. Last minute changes rarely can be tested, and if done quickly are more likely to contain mistakes.
    TVC-REQ-044
    L2. Flight Software Changes
    UID: TVC-REQ-044
    Level: L2
    Requirement type: Functional
    Applicable subsystem: Flight_Software
    Subteam owner: Software
    Individual owner: Software Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: Pre-Launch
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Inspection
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-REQ-043 No last Minute Changes
    Statement:

    The flight software and supporting systems that the rocket will use shall prevent changes less than 0.5 weeks before the expected launch date. Tracking for flight software shall be done using github, and no commits from after the 0.5 week cutoff shall be used in the flight software for launch. For each version of flight software that is flown on a rocket, it must be tagged in Github with the flight number. (Tag: Flight #).
    Rationale:

    This requirement decomposes the parent requirement to require a specific cutoff for changes to the flight software, along with requiring tags to improve traceability.
    TVC-REQ-045
    L1. Flight Computer Controls Ability
    UID: TVC-REQ-045
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Functional
    Applicable subsystem: Avionics, Flight_Software
    Subteam owner: Electrical
    Individual owner: Electrical Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: Powered Ascent
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: TBD
    Resolution owner: Controls
    Resolution plan: Need to find required control loop update rate, Requirement TVC-REQ-047 lists the full completion plan to get this value.
    Resolution due date: Refer to TVC-REQ-047
    Verification method: Test
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-009 Closed Loop Controls
    Statement:

    The flight computer shall be capable of running the controls algorithm at the required rate (Refer to TVC-REQ-047). It must also include all required minimum sensors and be able to read sensor data. Minimum sensors: IMU, Magnetometer, Barometer, GPS
    Rationale:

    In order to run on-board controls, the flight computer must do so. It shall not be a limiting factor for the control loop rate. The flight computer also must have the required sensors to do GNC.
    TVC-REQ-046
    L1. Flight Computer TVC Ability
    UID: TVC-REQ-046
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Functional
    Applicable subsystem: Avionics, Flight_Software, Actuation
    Subteam owner: Electrical
    Individual owner: Electrical Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: Powered Ascent
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: TBR
    Resolution owner: Controls lead
    Resolution plan: Once controls has resolved the minimum Gimbal Velocity, this help establish how quickly the update rate of the gimbal must be. Refer to TVC-REQ-006 for a more detailed resolution plan.
    Resolution due date: Refer to TVC-REQ-006
    Verification method: Test
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-009 Closed Loop Controls
    RELATIONS (Child):
    • TVC-REQ-048 Sensor Update Rate
    Statement:

    The flight computer shall be capable of controlling the actuators for the gimbal. It shall be able to send commands in order to meet minimum requirements for speed of the gimbal (TVC-REQ-006), [TBD_GimbalVelocity]
    Rationale:

    The flight computer must be able to control the gimbal to allow for effective closed loop on-board controls.
    TVC-REQ-047

    The flight software loop shall run at a minimum of [TBD_UpdateRate] Hz.
    Rationale:

    Need to have a minumum control loop run in order to ensure the TVC is reacting quickly enough.
    TVC-REQ-048
    L2. Sensor Update Rate
    UID: TVC-REQ-048

    Applicable subsystem: Avionics, Flight_Software
    Subteam owner: Software

    Statement:

    All sensors shall have a minumum udpate rate of [TBD_UpdateRate] Hz.
    Rationale:

    Controls requires a minimum update rate of the control loop, and the controllers must follow this update rate to support this control loop rate.
    TVC-REQ-049
    L1. Kalman Filter Usage
    UID: TVC-REQ-049
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Functional
    Applicable subsystem: Avionics, Flight_Software
    Subteam owner: Software, Controls
    Individual owner: Software Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: Powered Ascent
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Demonstration
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-009 Closed Loop Controls
    Statement:

    The flight software shall implement a Kalman filter for state estimation.
    Rationale:

    Kalman filter is an industry standard method of improving the accuracy of state estimation, which will improve the quality of the rocket closed loop controls.
    TVC-REQ-050
    L1. Flight Algorithm Stability
    UID: TVC-REQ-050
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Performance
    Applicable subsystem: Avionics, Flight_Software
    Subteam owner: Controls
    Individual owner: Controls Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1
    Mission phase: Powered Ascent
    Flight attempt: All
    Open item status: None
    Verification method: Analysis
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-001 Maintain Powered Attitude
    Statement:

    The controls algorithm shall be demonstratably stable over the course of the rockt's flight, within the expected controls range (Max angle of attack before controls is turned off).
    Rationale:

    In order to effectively stabilize the rocket, the flight algorithm must be stable over the course of the flight. Oscillations, exponential increases, etc... are all indicative of non-stable controls algorithm.
    TVC-REQ-051
    L1. Controls algorithm delay
    UID: TVC-REQ-051
    Level: L1
    Requirement type: Functional
    Applicable subsystem: Avionics, Flight_Software
    Subteam owner: Software, Controls
    Individual owner: Software Lead
    Vehicle configuration: TVC-F1

    Flight attempt: Flights 1-3
    Open item status: TBR
    Resolution owner: Structures
    Resolution plan: Waiting for a decision on launch rail height. Once rail height has been found, need to research how to simulate launch rail friction/loads for rocket, to find how long it would take the rocket to clear the rail.
    Resolution due date: November 30th
    Verification method: Demonstration
    Status: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • TVC-MO-013 Control Initial Delay
    Statement:

    The controls algorithm shall be delayed by [TBD_DelaySeconds] after launch is detected, before active controls are activated.
    Rationale:

    Need to set a specific delay before the rocket begins controlling the gimbal, in order for the rocket to clear the rail before starting active controls. Use rail length to determine the length.
